newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO to open new round of peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO to open new round of peace talks.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian peace teams return to the bargaining table on Sunday for a fresh round of negotiations on expanding Palestinian self-rule.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) chief negotiator Mahmoud Abbas were due to convene eight joint committees to tackle outstanding issues from a 1995 interim peace deal.
"We hope there will be quick achievements," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Jenin in the West Bank.

The stage for the talks was set when Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met last week to follow up a U.S.-brokered breakthrough allowing the Palestinians to take over most of the West Bank town of Hebron.

The agenda, set by a U.S. annex to the Hebron deal, covers arrangements for Palestinian sea and air ports, a "safe passage" between the West Bank and Gaza, economic, civil and financial affairs and "people to people" cooperation.

Arafat, despite the momentum created by the Hebron handover and Israel's release of 30 Palestinian women prisoners last week, warned Israel not to "gamble" with peace by expanding Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land.
"The current Israeli government gambles with the peace process if settlement activity is increased," he said.
About 130,000 Jews now live among more than two million Palestinians in settlements built in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which were both captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Netanyahu, who is visiting the United States, faces growing dissent from his own Likud party and right-wing coalition partners who say he must accelerate building projects for Jews in the West Bank and Arab East Jerusalem.

Arafat called on Israel to respect a March 7 deadline for the first of three planned Israeli withdrawals from West Bank rural areas slated to end by mid-1998. "We hope that Israel will implement its promises," he said.

Palestinians fear Israel will speed up the expansion of the Jewish settlements to impose facts on the ground in advance of the future pullbacks and "final status" peace talks, due to commence next month.
